Another easy extension of this idea is replacing the `GET_MEM` macro with two proper template functions, for example

`variant_internal.h`
```C++
template <typename T>
_FORCE_INLINE_ static T *get_value(Variant *v) { return reinterpret_cast<T *>(v->_data._mem); }
template <typename T>
_FORCE_INLINE_ static const T *get_value(const Variant *v) { return reinterpret_cast<const T *>(v->_data._mem); }
```

This cleans up the function calls, making them type safe in a way that macros can't ensure, and allows for making the underlying `Variant` class more flexible to work with. This is due to negating the need of adding another two functions to the accessor pile when Variant wants to support another type, for instance sets.

I worked on this conversion a little bit and ran successful tests on them thus far.  b765918dbe35dfcea0e9ce030033259a7956cacc

I'm with you to refactor Variant to be more streamlined and have less duplicate logic!

I recently had the honour of adding [variant_internal.h to godot-cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-cpp/blob/master/include/godot_cpp/variant/variant_internal.hpp). I realized a lot of the variant_internal boilerplate can be reduced with a `VariantInternalType` template struct. If I were to refactor variant_internal, trying to get rid of unnecessary overhead, this is the tool I would go for again. I'm not a big fan of macros (e.g. for switches) if they can be avoided because they obscure actual code structure (as opposed to templates, which just look like function calls).
